Read in rural and urban data with segments
```{r}
rural_seg <- readRDS("LCA/Round2/9b_dhs.seg_reform_rural_seg.rds")
urban_seg <- readRDS("LCA/Round2/9b_dhs.seg_reform_urban_seg.rds")
#dim(rural_seg) #23075   315
#dim(urban_seg) #26234   315

#Rename the cluster_k3
rural_seg <- rural_seg %>%
  dplyr::rename(k3 = cluster_k3) %>%
  mutate(k3 = recode(k3, `3` = "R1", `2` = "R2", `1` = "R3"))
rural_seg <- subset(rural_seg, select = -c(cluster_k2, cluster_k4, cluster_k5))
#dim(rural_seg) #23075   312
#table(rural_seg$k3) #R1(6036),R2(8794),R3(8245) 

urban_seg <- urban_seg %>%
  dplyr::rename(k3 = cluster_k3) %>%
  mutate(k3 = recode(k3, `3` = "U1", `1` = "U2", `2` = "U3"))
urban_seg <- subset(urban_seg, select = -c(cluster_k2, cluster_k4, cluster_k5))
#dim(urban_seg) #26234   312
#table(urban_seg$k3) # U1(9058),U2(8391),U3(8785)

# rbind urban and rural
dhs.seg.comb <- rbind(rural_seg, urban_seg)
#dim(dhs.seg.comb) #49309 (same as earlier after dropping duplicates)  312
```

```{r}
HH$v001<-HH$hv001
HH$v002<-HH$hv002
IR$wt<-IR$v005/1000000

HH <- HH %>% 
  mutate(cook.fuel = case_when(
    hv226 == 1 ~ "Electricity",
    hv226 == 2 ~ "LPG",
    hv226 == 3 ~ "Natural gas",
    hv226 == 5 ~ "Kerosene",
    hv226 == 8 ~ "Wood",
    hv226 == 95 ~ "No food cooked",
    TRUE ~ "Other"))

IR.merge <- IR %>% select(v001, v002, caseid, v501, v213, m15_1, m13_1, m14_1, s428aa_1, s428ab_1, s428ac_1, s428ad_1, s428ae_1, s428af_1, s428ag_1, s428ah_1, s428aa_2, s428ab_2, s428ac_2, s428ad_2, s428ae_2, s428af_2, s428ag_2, s428ah_2, v312, v313, v359)
#dim(IR.merge) #49627     24
HH.merge <- HH %>% select(v001, v002, cook.fuel, hv237, hv237a, hv237b, hv237c, hv237d, hv237e, hv237f, hv204)
#dim(HH.merge) #47963     10
newmerge <-merge(IR.merge, HH.merge, by=c("v001", "v002"), all.x=T)
#dim(newmerge) #49627    32
#newmerge$caseid
#dhs.seg.comb$caseid
dhs.seg.comb <- merge(dhs.seg.comb, newmerge, by="caseid", all.x=T)
#dim(dhs.seg.comb) #49309   343

#table(dhs.seg.comb$insurance.cov.cat1)
#table(dhs.seg.comb$hh.toilet.flush)
```

```{r, echo=TRUE}
dhs.seg.comb$k3 <- factor(dhs.seg.comb$k3)
dhs.seg.comb.des <-svydesign(id=~v021, strata=~v023, weights=~wt, data=dhs.seg.comb)
#In the following cases, I will apply survey design after specific data manipulation (e.g., filter, mutate). The survey weight is applied when we want to make inferences about the entire population from the sample data, and it is used to adjust for the survey's sampling design, such as unequal probabilities of selection, nonresponse, and stratification.

#Note that after apply survey weight, we may see decimals in frequency table. In survey analysis, weights reflect the number of units in the population that each sample unit represents. The weights can be any positive number, but not necessarily an integer. 
```

## 1. Segment Distribution & Demographics
```{r, echo=TRUE}
#Note (Feb 2024): after the Seattle Workshop, we considered segmenting it differently: for instance, women with children will be separet from women without. To further decided which sample(s) we should use to segment, first explore the sample sizes (with children vs without children), and look at the distribution of outcome variables (separate outcome and behavior) for different samples.
```

### 1.1. Overview
```{r}
seg.tab <- svytable(~k3, design = dhs.seg.comb.des)
seg.pie <- as.data.frame(seg.tab)

seg.pie <- seg.pie %>%
  mutate(percent = round((Freq / sum(Freq)) * 100, digits = 0),
         type = ifelse(substr(k3, 1, 1) == "R", "Rural", "Urban"))%>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(k3)) %>%
  mutate(cumulative_freq = cumsum(Freq),
         midpoint = cumulative_freq - (Freq/2))

# Define the color palette
rural_palette <- c("#ffd9b2ff", "#f5b068ff", "#f18619ff")
urban_palette <- c("#e5f0feff", "#99c4ff", "#002d8f5f")
palette <- c("Rural" = "#f18619ff", "Urban" = "#002d8f5f")
seg_colors <- setNames(c(rural_palette, urban_palette), unique(dhs.seg.comb$k3))

ggplot(seg.pie, aes(x = factor(1), fill = k3)) + 
  geom_bar(aes(weight = Freq), width = 1) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") + 
  geom_text(aes(y = midpoint, label = paste0(round(percent, 1), "%")), color = "black", size = 3.5) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = seg_colors) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Segment") +
  theme_void() +
  ggtitle("Segment Distribution")

seg.pie
```

### 1.2. Distribution within province
```{r, fig.height=7}
#4 focus district: Garut (in West Java, 32 in hv024), Badung (in Bali, 51 in hv024), Pidie (in Aceh, 11 in hv024) and Sambuwa Barat (in west nusa tenggara, 52 in hv024). For hv024, it is province level. The focus is district level.

#9601 rows (19.5%) for these 4 provinces
seg.location <- dhs.seg.comb %>% 
  filter(hv024 == 32 | hv024 == 51 | hv024 == 11 | hv024 == 52) %>% 
  mutate(province = case_when(
    hv024 == 32 ~ "West Java (Garut)",
    hv024 == 51 ~ "Bali (Badung)",
    hv024 == 11 ~ "Aceh (Pidie)",
    hv024 == 52 ~ "West Nusa Tenggara (Sambuwa Barat)"))

seg.location.des <-svydesign(id=~v021, strata=~v023, weights=~wt, data=seg.location)
seg.prov <- svytable(~k3 + province, design = seg.location.des)
seg.prov <- as.data.frame(seg.prov)

seg.prov <- seg.prov %>%
  group_by(province) %>% 
  mutate(perc = round((Freq / sum(Freq)) * 100, digits = 0)) %>% 
  ungroup()

ggplot(seg.prov, aes(x = province, y = perc, fill = k3)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack", width = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(perc, "%")), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 3.5) +
  labs(x = "Province", y = "Percentage", fill = "Segment", title = "Segment Distribution within Selected Provinces") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#9cc2f4", "#386CB0","#03859b","#b590bf","#8E24AA","#563880","#bf281c")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5))

seg.prov
```

### 1.3. Age by segment
```{r}
#the thick bar represents the median value
# Calculate the median age by segment (k3) using the survey package
median_age <- svyby(~age.yrs, ~k3, dhs.seg.comb.des, svyquantile, quantiles = c(0.5), na.rm = TRUE)
median_age <- median_age %>% rename(median_age = age.yrs)

# Calculate the first and third quartiles
q1_age <- svyby(~age.yrs, ~k3, dhs.seg.comb.des, svyquantile, quantiles = c(0.25), na.rm = TRUE)
q1_age <- q1_age %>%  rename(q1 = age.yrs)
q3_age <- svyby(~age.yrs, ~k3, dhs.seg.comb.des, svyquantile, quantiles = c(0.75), na.rm = TRUE)
q3_age <- q3_age %>%  rename(q3 = age.yrs)
min_age <- svyby(~age.yrs, ~k3, dhs.seg.comb.des, svyquantile, quantiles = c(0.0), na.rm = TRUE)
min_age <- min_age %>% rename(min = age.yrs)
max_age <- svyby(~age.yrs, ~k3, dhs.seg.comb.des, svyquantile, quantiles = c(1.0), na.rm = TRUE)
max_age <- max_age %>% rename(max = age.yrs)

age_stats <- full_join(q1_age, q3_age, by = "k3")
age_stats <- full_join(age_stats, median_age, by = "k3")
age_stats <- full_join(age_stats, min_age, by = "k3")
age_stats <- full_join(age_stats, max_age, by = "k3")

age_stats <- age_stats %>% 
  select("k3", "min", "q1", "median_age", "q3", "max")

ggplot(age_stats, aes(x = k3, y = median_age)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(lower = q1, upper = q3, middle = median_age, ymin = min, ymax = max), stat = "identity", fill = "grey80", color = "black", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(median_age, 1), y = median_age), position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), vjust = -0.5, color = "black", size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = seg_colors) + 
  labs(x = "Segment", y = "Age", title = "Age Distribution by Segment") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

age_stats
```

### 1.4. Women pregnancy history
```{r}
#3 groups for women: (1)women who have children of any age (2) women who are pregnant (3) women without children and who are not pregnant 
  #need to select v213 from IR and merge with dhs.seg.comb
 #v213 == 1 ~ "Pregnant" (0 ~ no or unsure) #question 226: Are you pregnant now? (yes, no, dk)
#dhs.seg.comb$v213 #0=no or unsure, 1=yes
#dhs.seg.comb$v201: Total number of children ever born
#table(dhs.seg.comb$v201)
#sum(15361,8589,23068,21774,14148,7780,4386,2562,1744,801,370,220,120,39) #100962
seg.woman <- dhs.seg.comb %>% 
  mutate(with.kid = ifelse(v201 > 0, 1, 0)) %>% 
  mutate(woman.group = case_when(
    with.kid == 1 ~ "With child(ren)",
    (v213 == 1 & with.kid == 0) ~ "Without kid and pregnant",
    TRUE ~ "No kid nor pregnant"))

seg.woman.des <-svydesign(id=~v021, strata=~v023, weights=~wt, data=seg.woman)
seg.womgp <- svytable(~k3 + woman.group, design = seg.woman.des)
seg.womgp <- as.data.frame(seg.womgp)

seg.womgp <- seg.womgp %>% 
  group_by(k3) %>%
  mutate(perc = round((Freq/sum(Freq))*100, digits = 0)) %>%
  ungroup()

##recorder
seg.womgp$woman.group <- factor(seg.womgp$woman.group , levels = c("With child(ren)", "Without kid and pregnant", "No kid nor pregnant"),labels = c("With child(ren)", "Without kid and pregnant", "No kid nor pregnant"))

ggplot(seg.womgp, aes(x = k3, y = perc, fill = woman.group)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(perc, "%")), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = "Segment", y = "Percentage", fill = "Segment", title = "Distribution of Women within Segment") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#03859b", "#bf281c", "#b4adaa")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1))

seg.womgp
```

## 2. Differentiating Variables: Key Vunerability Measures Used in Clustering
### 2.1. Heatmap (binary)
```{r}
seg.k3 <- dhs.seg.comb %>% 
  select(c(bin.var),k3)

#dim(seg.k3)
seg.k3 <- seg.k3 %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(bin.var), ~ifelse(. == 2, 1, 0), .names = "prop_{.col}")) %>%
  group_by(k3) %>%
  summarise(across(starts_with("prop_"), mean)) 
seg.k3 <- seg.k3 %>% 
  mutate(area = ifelse(k3 == "R1" | k3 == "R2" | k3 == "R3", "Rural", "Urban"))
#view(seg.k3)

#define var.labels
custom_labels <- c(
  "marr.cohab" = "With partner",
  "early.cohab.19" = "Early marriage or cohabitation",
  "media.sum.2plus" = "Use 2+ media sources",
  "num.under15.2plus" = "With 2+ children U15",
  "hh.kidwom.rat.2plus" = "Ratio of U5 to women >=2",
  "husb.ed.mtprim" = "Partner edu more than primary",
  "highestyearsedinHH.7plus" = "7+ years of edu for HH",
  "hh.watpur.appr" = "Use water purify method",
  "hh.toilet.flush" = "Use flush toilet",
  "med.distance" = "Distance is a big problem",
  "med.alone" = "Going alone is a big problem",
  "med.permis" = "Getting permision is a big problem",
  "disc.fp.yn" = "Discuss FP with someone",
  "insurance.cov.cat1" = "Coverged by EPM insurance",
  "hh.land" = "Own land for agriculture"
)

# Reshape dataframe for ggplot
df_long <- seg.k3 %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("prop_"), names_to = "var.label", values_to = "prop") %>%
  mutate(var.label = str_remove(var.label, "prop_"),
         label = ifelse(var.label %in% names(custom_labels), custom_labels[var.label], var.label),
         label_percent = scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 1))
df_long <- merge(df_long, var, by.x = "var.label", by.y = "f.var.name")

df_long$category <- gsub("Woman and her past experiences", "Woman and her\npast experiences", df_long$category)
df_long$category <- gsub("Household relationships", "Household\nrelationships", df_long$category)
df_long$category <- gsub("Household economics and living conditions", "HH econ &\nliving cond.", df_long$category)
df_long$category <- gsub("Health mental models", "Health mental\nmodels", df_long$category)
df_long$category <- gsub("Social support", "Social\nsupport", df_long$category)
df_long$category <- gsub("Human and natural systems", "H&N\nsystem", df_long$category)

df_long$category <- factor(df_long$category, 
                    levels = c("Woman and her\npast experiences", "Household\nrelationships", "HH econ &\nliving cond.", "Health mental\nmodels","Social\nsupport","H&N\nsystem"),ordered = TRUE)

# Plot
ggplot(df_long, aes(x = factor(k3), y = label, fill = prop)) +
  geom_tile() +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(category), cols = vars(area), scales = "free", space = "free", switch = "y") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#313695", mid = "#FFFFBF", high = "#A50026", midpoint = 0.5, breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.1)) +
  labs(title = "Proportion within cluster", x = '', y = '', fill = 'Proportion within\ncluster') +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 5),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 5),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 6),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.placement = "outside",
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 180, size = 5), 
        panel.spacing.y = unit(0.8, "lines"))

#df_long
```

### 2.2. Stacked bar (categorical)
```{r}
#For categorical data, we need something different:
rural.seg.cat <- readRDS("LCA/Round2/9b_dhs.seg_rural_seg.rds")
urban.seg.cat <- readRDS("LCA/Round2/9b_dhs.seg_urban_seg.rds")
#dim(rural.seg.cat) #23075   315
#dim(urban.seg.cat) #26234   315

rural.seg.cat <- rural.seg.cat %>%
  dplyr::rename(k3 = cluster_k3) %>%
  mutate(k3 = recode(k3, `3` = "R1", `2` = "R2", `1` = "R3"))
rural.seg.cat <- subset(rural.seg.cat, select = -c(cluster_k2, cluster_k4, cluster_k5))
#dim(rural.seg.cat) #23075   312
#table(rural_seg$k3) #R1(6036), R2(8794), R3(8245)

urban.seg.cat <- urban.seg.cat %>%
  dplyr::rename(k3 = cluster_k3) %>%
  mutate(k3 = recode(k3, `3` = "U1", `1` = "U2", `2` = "U3"))
urban.seg.cat <- subset(urban.seg.cat, select = -c(cluster_k2, cluster_k4, cluster_k5))
#dim(urban.seg.cat) #26234   312
#table(urban.seg.cat$k3)  #U1(9058), U2(8391), U3(8785)

# rbind urban and rural
dhs.seg.comb.cat <- rbind(rural.seg.cat, urban.seg.cat)
dhs.seg.comb.cat <- merge(dhs.seg.comb.cat, newmerge, by="caseid", all.x=T)
#dim(dhs.seg.comb.cat) #49309   343
```

```{r, fig.height = 8, fig.width=20}
# Prepare data
dhs.seg.comb <- dhs.seg.comb %>% 
  mutate(slum1 = case_when(
    slum1 == 1 ~ "rural",
    slum1 == 2 ~ "urban non-slum",
    TRUE ~ "urban slum"))

custom_labels <- c(
  "ed.lev.cat1" = "Women's edu",
  "wd.ownincome.cat" = "Women's deicision on own income",
  "jd.hlth.cat" = "Joined decision on women's health",
  "work.seasonal" = "Women's work",
  "water.cat" = "Water source",
  "partner.working" = "Partner's work",
  "auto.contra" = "Autonomy on contraceptive",
  "vehic.index" = "Vehicle ownership",
  "slum1" = "Slum or not"
)

#table(dhs.seg.comb$slum1)

long_dt <- dhs.seg.comb.cat %>%
  select(c(cat.var, 'k3')) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(cat.var), names_to = "variable", values_to = "level")

cluster_size <- long_dt %>%
  group_by(k3, variable) %>%
  summarize(cluster_total = n(), .groups = 'drop')

agg_dt <- long_dt %>%
  group_by(k3, variable, level) %>%
  summarize(ct = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>% 
  left_join(cluster_size, by = c("k3", "variable")) %>% 
  mutate(pct = round((ct/cluster_total)*100, 2)) %>% 
  mutate(var.label = ifelse(variable %in% names(custom_labels), 
                            custom_labels[variable], 
                            variable))

agg_dt <- merge(agg_dt, var, by.x = "variable", by.y = "f.var.name")

agg_dt$category <- gsub("Woman and her past experiences", "Woman and her\npast experiences", agg_dt$category)
agg_dt$category <- gsub("Household relationships", "Household\nrelationships", agg_dt$category)
agg_dt$category <- gsub("Household economics and living conditions", "HH econ &\nliving cond.", agg_dt$category)
agg_dt$category <- gsub("Health mental models", "Health mental\nmodels", agg_dt$category)
agg_dt$category <- gsub("Social support", "Social\nsupport", agg_dt$category)
agg_dt$category <- gsub("Human and natural systems", "H&N\nsystem", agg_dt$category)

agg_dt$category <- factor(agg_dt$category, 
                    levels = c("Woman and her\npast experiences", "Household\nrelationships", "HH econ &\nliving cond.", "Health mental\nmodels","Social\nsupport","H&N\nsystem"),ordered = TRUE)

agg_dt$var.label <- gsub("Women's edu", "Women's edu", agg_dt$var.label)
agg_dt$var.label <- gsub("Women's deicision on own income", "Women's deicision\non own income", agg_dt$var.label)
agg_dt$var.label <- gsub("Joined decision on women's health", "Joined decision\non women's health", agg_dt$var.label)
agg_dt$var.label <- gsub("Women's work", "Women's work", agg_dt$var.label)
agg_dt$var.label <- gsub("Water source", "Water source", agg_dt$var.label)
agg_dt$var.label <- gsub("Partner's work", "Partner's work", agg_dt$var.label)
agg_dt$var.label <- gsub("Autonomy on contraceptive", "Autonomy on\ncontraceptive", agg_dt$var.label)
agg_dt$var.label <- gsub("Vehicle ownership", "Vehicle\nownership", agg_dt$var.label)

#view(agg_dt)
agg_dt <- agg_dt %>% 
  mutate(area = ifelse(k3 == "R1" | k3 == "R2" | k3 == "R3", "Rural", "Urban"))

# Define a manual color palette
my_colors <- c("0" = "#f9c696", "1" = "#FDB863" , "2" = "#BF5B17", "Full or partial autonomy" = "#ECEC26", "No control over" = "#FFFF99", "Not partnered" = "#F0027F", "Higher education" = "#386CB0", "Some eduction" = "#9cc2f4", "No eduction" = "#666666", "Not in union" = "#F0027F", "Not paid in cash or not working" = "#e0dcdc", "No" = "#666666","Yes" = "#D32F2F", "Not protected" = "#666666", "Open protected" = "#C7E9C0",  "Piped or borehole" = "#7FC97F", "Tank or packed" = "#259d25", "All  year" = "#563880", "Seasonal" = "#BEAED4", "Occassional" = "#e6dff1", "No work in the past 12 months" = "#666666", "Worked last 12 months" = "#8E24AA", "Worked last 7 days" = "#b590bf", "Not working or no partner"="#F0027F","rural" = "#ffd9b2ff", "urban non-slum" = "#f2a273f5", "urban slum" = "#d46f32f5")

# Plot
ggplot(agg_dt, aes(x=var.label, y=pct, fill=level)) + 
  geom_bar(stat="identity", position="stack",width=0.5) + 
  facet_grid(category ~ k3, scales = "free_y", space = "free_x", switch = "y") + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(scale = 1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=my_colors) +
  labs(title = "Distribution within cluster", x = "", y = "Percentage of cluster total") +
  guides(fill=guide_legend(title="Level")) +
  geom_text(aes(label=round(pct, 0)), position=position_stack(vjust=0.5), size=3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  coord_flip()  +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.placement = "outside",
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6, angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5.5),
        panel.spacing = unit(0.1, "lines"), 
        strip.text = element_text(size = 6))

#agg_dt
```

#### 3.3.1. Number of ANC
```{r}
#"anc.num": number of ANC during the pregnancy
median_anc <- svyby(~anc.num, ~k3, dhs.seg.comb.des, svyquantile, quantiles = c(0.5), na.rm = TRUE)
median_anc <- median_anc %>% rename(median_anc = anc.num)

q1_anc <- svyby(~anc.num, ~k3, dhs.seg.comb.des, svyquantile, quantiles = c(0.25), na.rm = TRUE)
q1_anc <- q1_anc %>%  rename(q1 = anc.num)
q3_anc <- svyby(~anc.num, ~k3, dhs.seg.comb.des, svyquantile, quantiles = c(0.75), na.rm = TRUE)
q3_anc <- q3_anc %>%  rename(q3 = anc.num)
min_anc <- svyby(~anc.num, ~k3, dhs.seg.comb.des, svyquantile, quantiles = c(0.0), na.rm = TRUE)
min_anc <- min_anc %>% rename(min = anc.num)
max_anc <- svyby(~anc.num, ~k3, dhs.seg.comb.des, svyquantile, quantiles = c(1.0), na.rm = TRUE)
max_anc <- max_anc %>% rename(max = anc.num)

anc_stats <- full_join(q1_anc, q3_anc, by = "k3")
anc_stats <- full_join(anc_stats, median_anc, by = "k3")
anc_stats <- full_join(anc_stats, min_anc, by = "k3")
anc_stats <- full_join(anc_stats, max_anc, by = "k3")
anc_stats <- anc_stats %>% 
  select("k3", "min", "q1", "median_anc", "q3", "max")

ggplot(anc_stats, aes(x = k3, y = median_anc)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(lower = q1, upper = q3, middle = median_anc, ymin = min, ymax = max), stat = "identity", fill = "grey80", color = "black", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(median_anc, 1), y = median_anc), position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), vjust = 1.5, color = "black", size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = seg_colors) + 
  labs(x = "Segment", y = "Numer of ANC Attendance", title = "Distribution of Number of ANC Attendance by Segment") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

anc_stats
```

#### 3.3.2. ANC attendance category

```{r}
seg.anc.cat <- dhs.seg.comb %>%
```

### 3.4. Birth complication
```{r, echo=TRUE}
#base: "women who had child born in the last 5 years"
```

```{r, echo=TRUE}
#IR[,bc.1:= ifelse(s428aa_1== 1 | s428ab_1== 1 | s428ac_1== 1 | s428ad_1== 1 | s428ae_1== 1 | s428af_1== 1 | s428ag_1 == 1 | s428ah_1== 1,1,0)]
#IR[,bc.2:= ifelse(s428aa_2== 1 | s428ab_2== 1 | s428ac_2== 1 | s428ad_2== 1 | s428ae_2== 1 | s428af_2== 1 | s428ag_2 == 1 | s428ah_2== 1,1,0)]
#0==no, 1==yes, 8==don't know

#aa:PROLONGED LABOR; ab:VAGINAL BLEEDING; ac: A high fever and foul smelling vaginal discharge; ad:Convulsions; ae: water breaks; af: no strength to press; ag: anxious/in pain; ah: other

#prolonged labor and anxious/in pain are most common 

#table(IR$s428aa_1)
#table(IR$s428ab_1)
#table(IR$s428ac_1)
#table(IR$s428ad_1)
#table(IR$s428ae_1)
#table(IR$s428af_1)
#table(IR$s428ag_1)
#table(IR$s428ah_1)

#table(IR$s428aa_2)
#table(IR$s428ab_2)
#table(IR$s428ac_2)
#table(IR$s428ad_2)
#table(IR$s428ae_2)
#table(IR$s428af_2)
#table(IR$s428ag_2)
#table(IR$s428ah_2)

dhs.seg.comb <- dhs.seg.comb %>%
  mutate(bc.new = case_when(
    (bc.ever == 0) ~ "No birth complication",
    (is.na(bc.ever) ~ NA),
    (s428aa_1== 1 | s428aa_2== 1) ~ "Prolonged labor",
    TRUE ~ "Other types of birth complications"
  ))

#table(dhs.seg.comb$bc.new)
#table(dhs.seg.comb$bc.ever)
```

### 3.5. Use of modern FP
```{r, echo=TRUE}
#This question was asked to all women.
  #0=	not using (pregnant women were coded as 0 too), 1=pill, 2=IUD, 3=injections 3 month, 5=male condom, 6=female sterilization, 7=male sterilization, 8=periodic abstinence, 9=withdrawal, 10=other traditional, 11=implants/norplant, 13=lactational amenorrhea (lam), 19=injection 1 months, 
  #Note that some DHS standard FP options were not used or chosen in IND suryve, like: 14=female condom, 15=foam or jelly, 16=emergency contraception, 17=other modern method, 18=standard days method (sdm), 20=specific method 2
#table(dhs.seg.comb$v312)

#I categorized it as below:
  ##Traditional Methods: 8=Periodic abstinence, 9=Withdrawal, 10=Other traditional methods, 13=Lactational amenorrhea 
  ##Modern Methods:
    ###Short-acting Methods: 1=Pill, 3=Injections 3 month, 5=Male condom, 19=Injection 1 month 
    ###Long-acting Methods: 2=IUD, 6=Female sterilization, 7=Male sterilization, 11=Implants/Norplant

#For v359 in Indonesia (used in the last 5 years but not now): 1=pill, 2=IUD, 3=injections 3 month, 5=male condom, 6=female sterilization, 7=male sterilization, 8=periodic abstinence, 9=withdrawal, 10=other traditional, 11=implants/norplant, 13=lactational amenorrhea (lam). Re-categorized as:
  ##Traditional Methods: 8=Periodic abstinence, 9=Withdrawal, 10=Other traditional methods, 13=Lactational amenorrhea 
  ##Modern Methods:
    ###Short-acting Methods: 1=Pill, 3=Injections 3 month, 5=Male condom
    ###Long-acting Methods: 2=IUD, 6=Female sterilization, 7=Male sterilization, 11=Implants/Norplant
```

```{r}
#construct: fp.ever.new
dhs.seg.comb <- dhs.seg.comb %>% 
  mutate(fp.now.new = case_when(
    (v312 == 8 | v312 == 9 | v312 == 10 | v312 == 13) ~ "Traditional FP methods",
    (v312 == 1 | v312 == 3 | v312 == 5 | v312 == 19) ~ "Modern short-acting",
    (v312 == 2 | v312 == 6 | v312 == 7 | v312 == 11) ~ "Modern long-acting",
    (v312 == 0 | is.na(v312)) ~ "Not using",
  ))
#table(dhs.seg.comb$fp.now.new)

dhs.seg.comb <- dhs.seg.comb %>% 
  mutate(fp.past.new = case_when(
    (v359 == 8 | v359 == 9 | v359 == 10 | v359 == 13) ~ "Traditional FP methods",
    (v359 == 1 | v359 == 3 | v359 == 5) ~ "Modern short-acting",
    (v359 == 2 | v359 == 6 | v359 == 7 | v359 == 11) ~ "Modern long-acting",
    (v359 == 0 | is.na(v359)) ~ "Not using",
  ))
#table(dhs.seg.comb$fp.past.new)
```

## 4. Deep Dive: Defining Variables
```{r, echo=TRUE}
#In this section, we plot defining variables: they are from the exploratory analysis, in which we examined the associations between ~ 190 variables (from script 4) and the outcome variables. The exploratory analysis (and exploration of the association between some of them and age) eventually suggested 86 unique variables. 
  ##Note that for the ~ 190 variables, some of them were constructed for the same "vulnerability measures". For instance, there were ~ 4-5 variables contrscuted around number of pregnancies. We constructed multiple variables for the same measure to explore variables cut-offs and compare the overall model fit and patterns.

#These 86 variables were then mapped to the 6 domains (and the respective constructs under the domain), see the spreadhseet named "7_Construct_mapping", Sheet1. Note that a variable may be mapped to multiple constructs or domains. Therefore, in Sheet 1, you will see 98 rows.

#Among the 86 variables, 21 of them were brought to LCA for clustering, based on the results from PCA. The plots for the 21 variables can be found in section 2 above.

#This section will plot the remaining 65, organized by the domain and construct.
```

#### 4.1.2. Internalized gender norms
##### 4.1.2.1. Perception of domestic violence (dv.index.2)
```{r, echo=TRUE}
#This comes from the question: in your opinion, is a husband justified in hitting or beating his wife in the following situations: v744a: She goes out without telling him; v744b: She neglects the children; v744c: She argues with him; v744d: She refuses to have sex with him; v744e: She burns the food. For each situation, it was coded as "1" if "yes"; then it summed up. The sum ranges from 0 to 5. If the sum is 2, 3, 4, 5, it was coded as "1" for dv.index.2. That is saying, "Yes" here means the woman perceives the domestic violence as justified
```


##### 4.2.2.13. Joined decision index (jd.index.cat)
```{r, echo=TRUE}
#for decision-making index, out of the 6 scenarios, we grouped it into "1-3" (e.g. "yes" in making decision in 1-3 scenarios), "4-6", "not in union", and "none"
#one scenario is not included above, which is about childnre's health - it shows low overall model fit and unclear patterns during exploratory analysis.

#from the following 2 plots, we can see that joint decision-making does not enhance women's decision-making autonomy.
```

```{r}
#table(dhs.seg.comb$jd.index.cat) #Four to six,None, Not in union, One to three 
dhs.seg.comb$jd.index.cat <- as.factor(dhs.seg.comb$jd.index.cat)

seg.jd.index.des <-svydesign(id=~v021, strata=~v023, weights=~wt, data= dhs.seg.comb)
seg.jd.index <- svytable(~k3 + jd.index.cat, design = seg.jd.index.des)
seg.jd.index <- as.data.frame(seg.jd.index)

seg.jd.index <- seg.jd.index %>% 
  group_by(k3) %>%
  mutate(perc = round((Freq/sum(Freq))*100, digits = 0)) %>%
  ungroup()

##recorder
seg.jd.index$jd.index.cat <- factor(seg.jd.index$jd.index.cat, levels = c("Four to six", "One to three", "None", "Not in union"),labels = c("Four to six", "One to three", "None", "Not in union"))
```
